defects.title: Every injury row was attributed to Dallas Cowboys
defects.found: By counting distinct clubs in data/lines/injuries.json while reviewing the injury tracker: 296 rows, 1 club.
defects.impact: All 296 rows of the official Week 10 report carried team = 'Dallas Cowboys'. The row values (player, position, injury, practice, game status) were right; the club was wrong on every row, and the lineup-risk table built from it named one club's players against every fixture.
defects.fix: The parser searched the whole preceding page for a full club name and kept the last match, so every table inherited the club named last. It now binds each table to its own club title element. The rebuilt file matches the independent parse in data/nfl-analytics/injuries-week-10-2026.json on all 296 rows.

defects.title: leaderboard.json disagreed with strategies.json on the reward for S03
defects.found: By comparing the two published files field by field while reviewing the strategy board.
defects.impact: strategies.json gave S03 a reward of 72; leaderboard.json gave 0. The whole leaderboard was built from copies taken before the redundancy gate ran, so the gate's rewrite of G7, status and reward never reached the published leaderboard, and its ranks were computed before G7 applied.
defects.fix: Leaderboard rows are now the same objects as the strategy rows, with an assertion that fails the build on any drift. S03 is published as failed on both files, with reward 0.

defects.title: The published shuffle test could only return p = 1.000
defects.found: By re-deriving the statistic from the committed outcomes while recomputing the published home-field figures.
defects.impact: The test permuted 453 outcomes and compared the permuted home-win count with the observed count. A permutation cannot change that count, so p was 1.0000 by construction. The conclusion it supported happens to be correct, but the test could not have failed.
defects.fix: Replaced with a two-sided bootstrap on the hit indicator: 0.5121 observed, 95% interval 0.4702-0.5607, p = 0.6657. Same conclusion, real test.

defects.title: All 14 Week 10 games were stored sixteen times each
defects.found: By counting duplicate game ids in data/lines/games.json while reviewing the lineup-risk table, after noticing the same Detroit rows repeated on the live page.
defects.impact: 482 regular-season 2026 rows for 272 unique games. The published '1,170 games' count was inflated (true figure 960), and the lineup table listed every deficiency nine times.
defects.fix: fetch_games() now de-duplicates by game id at fetch time; the committed capture was rebuilt the same way and every derived file regenerated. Lineup rows: 207 -> 75.

defects.title: A backup was named from the wrong row of the club's depth chart
defects.found: By re-reading Detroit's official chart against the published replacement: the page said Ennis Rakestraw Jr., the chart row says Rock Ya-Sin.
defects.impact: The builder searched the whole position and took the alphabetically first player at the next tier, so a corner from a different chart row was named as the next man up. 26 rows name a replacement.
defects.fix: Chart rows are recovered (a new row starts at each '1st' tier) and the replacement is taken from the injured player's own row, with a sameChartRow field published. Verified live on Detroit and New England.

flags.detail: Across 137 verified 2026 finals the weighted home-field edge is −0.02 points per game — far below the historically assumed ~2.5 points. The model uses the computed value. Whether this is a season quirk, a schedule artifact or a lasting change is unverified (see Q-HFA).

flags.detail: The rest-days difference is the strongest measured pre-game signal against 2026 margins (n=74 walk-forward). It is partially confounded: Week-12 bye teams carry a rest edge into their next game by construction. The predictive correlation is computed and reported; any causal interpretation is unverified.

flags.title: Parlay-leg and player-prop pair correlations are blank
flags.detail: The strategy frameworks need empirical joint-hit correlations to price same-game parlays and prop combos. No graded market or prop data exists in this system, so all such cells are blank and flagged; conservative Frechet bounds are documented as the interim policy (see Q-PROPS, Q-ODDS).

flags.title: No market prices in this repository: no edge, ROI or CLV claim is possible
flags.detail: The NFL Signals Lab publishes model lines only, each labelled 'model line - no market price exists in this repository to compare against'. Edge, ROI and closing-line value require archived odds with timestamps; no price feed is held here, so no such claim is made on any page. Adding a licensed, timestamped price archive is what would unblock them - not different wording.

flags.title: Availability data is one current snapshot, not a point-in-time archive
flags.detail: nfl.com/injuries/ returns identical markup for every season/week query, so the capture stores one dated snapshot per run. Applying today's report to past weeks would leak, so the injury-adjusted strategy's leakage gate is marked failed on purpose and its backtest figure is not comparable to the others. Point-in-time history accumulates through data/nfl-signals/forward-ledger.json, one archive per run.

flags.title: Five played 2026 games carry no score label on the official by-week page
flags.detail: For all five (each involving the same club) the by-week card renders a 'Watch Replay' link where the FINAL score label normally sits, and the game page itself publishes no score text either. Those rows stay null, are excluded from scoring, and are counted as pastGamesStillMissingScores in official/lab/fetch-report.json. The exact markup is preserved in official/lab/gap-context.json so a future parser fix is written against evidence instead of assumption.

flags.title: No official depth chart: replacement tiers cannot be computed
flags.detail: nfl.com/depth-charts/ and the per-club depth-chart paths return 404, and no payload on the captured pages carries a position-ranked depth chart. Second-, third- and fourth-string claims are therefore left uncomputed and listed in correlation_study.notComputable, rather than estimated from contract year or snap counts.

flags.title: Backtest sample cannot separate the models from luck
flags.detail: 100 games are scoreable out of sample from the 2026 capture. The paired difference between the leading strategy and the home-field baseline has t = 1.48 with a week-block bootstrap interval of [-0.005, 0.073], which includes zero, so the leaderboard is published as provisional and no prize is payable. Roughly 180 paired games would be needed at the observed effect size; the pre-registered promotion gate is 60 settled forward-ledger rows. Figures rendered on nfl-signals-backtest.html always come from the latest run.

flags.title: Standings payload carries no points for/against
flags.detail: The embedded by-week standings blob gives wins, losses, ties, home/away splits and division rank but no points columns, so standingsWithoutPoints is 32/32 and pointsFor/pointsAgainst stay null. Team points used by the model come from the game scores themselves and are never back-filled from another table.

flags.title: Inactives are reachable only through official articles
flags.detail: nfl.com/inactives/ is client-rendered (the capture's probe finds only an apiUrls entry), so the page yields zero rows and inactives are read from the weekly official inactives article, which exists for some weeks only. Because the 2026 rulebook sets a 48-player game-day active roster, an inactive is not necessarily injured; the two are kept as separate fields and never substituted for one another.

flags.title: Player-prop combinations are specified but uncomputed
flags.detail: No player-level season statistics and no prop prices are captured; the official player-statistics page renders client-side. propCombos.available is false, with the required inputs and the joint-distribution method written out so the analysis can run the day the data exists. No player-prop number is published in the meantime.

flags.title: The published shuffle test could not have returned anything but p = 1.000
flags.detail: nfl/system/tools/analyze_market.py permuted the 453 decided outcomes and compared the permuted home-win COUNT against the observed count (232). Permuting a list cannot change how many of its entries are 1, so the comparison was 232 >= 232 on every one of the 2,000 draws and the p-value was 1.0000 by construction. The conclusion it was used to support - that a home-field prior is not distinguishable from a coin at this sample - happens to be correct, and the README carried that sentence. The test itself was vacuous. Replaced on 2026-11-13 with a two-sided bootstrap on the per-game hit indicator: observed home win rate 0.5121 on 453 decided games, 95% bootstrap interval 0.4702-0.5607, p = 0.6657. That is a real test that reaches the same published conclusion.

sources.name: NFL.com official standings (outcomes only; no price data exists)
